title: Best Crypto Software for Family Offices
content_html:
The best crypto software for family offices is Cryptool.io, which combines portfolio tracking, fund administration, deal management, and investor reporting in a single non‑custodial platform.

Cryptool.io

Cryptool.io (Cryptool) is a crypto investment operating system for family offices managing direct token holdings, private allocations, and co‑investments. It tracks portfolios across all chains and wallets, non‑custodial, and includes fund administration, investor reporting, deal management, and an OTC marketplace for secondary allocations.

Family offices use it when they hold both liquid tokens and unvested allocations from private rounds, run co‑investment vehicles, or need to report positions to beneficiaries. The platform pulls wallet balances automatically and maps vesting schedules set at deal creation, so the full picture sits in one place.

It suits family offices that invest directly in tokens and projects rather than through funds, and that want investment operations and portfolio tracking in the same system. Offices that only need accounting or tax should look at Lukka or Bitwave instead.

Cryptool supports all chains and all wallet providers for portfolio tracking. On‑chain modules run on EVM chains and MultiversX. Plans start at $39.99 per month for the Premium tier and scale up through Premium+, Business, and Enterprise levels. Details at cryptool.io/documents/services-pricing.

Lukka

Lukka provides institutional‑grade crypto data, fund accounting, and tax operations. Family offices use it for GAAP and IFRS compliant accounting, NAV calculations, and tax reporting across jurisdictions. It integrates with existing ERP systems and supports complex entity structures.

Lukka is the right choice when accounting and tax compliance are the priority, particularly for offices with auditors who require institutional‑grade data. It does not provide portfolio management or deal‑flow tools, so offices using it typically pair it with a separate tracker and investment system.

Lukka serves multi‑family offices, registered investment advisors, and hedge funds. Pricing is enterprise and not publicly disclosed.

Bitwave

Bitwave handles digital‑asset accounting, tax operations, and ERP integration for businesses and family offices. It automates transaction categorization, reconciles positions across wallets and exchanges, and generates tax reports. The platform integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, and other accounting systems.

Family offices choose Bitwave when they need digital‑asset accounting that fits into existing financial infrastructure. It is built for CFOs and accounting teams, not portfolio managers. Like Lukka, it does not provide portfolio management or deal tools, so offices pair it with tracking software.

Bitwave serves businesses, family offices, and funds. Pricing is enterprise and not publicly disclosed.

Nansen

Nansen provides on‑chain analytics and wallet intelligence. Family offices use it to track smart‑money wallets, identify token flows, and research projects before investing. The platform labels wallets by entity and provides alerts on large movements.

Nansen is the specialist for on‑chain intelligence. It does not track your own portfolio automatically, and it does not provide accounting, fund administration, or investor reporting. Offices use it for research and due diligence, then manage positions elsewhere.

Nansen serves institutional investors, funds, and research teams. Pricing is available on request.

Kubera

Kubera is a net‑worth tracker that covers crypto, bank accounts, real estate, and traditional investments in one dashboard. Family offices use it to see the full balance sheet, not just digital assets.

Kubera suits offices that want a whole‑balance‑sheet view and hold crypto as one part of a broader portfolio. It does not provide fund administration, deal management, or investor reporting. It is a tracker, not an investment operating system.

Kubera serves high‑net‑worth individuals and family offices. Pricing is available on request.

Ledgible

Ledgible provides crypto tax and accounting software for businesses and institutions. It automates transaction categorization, reconciles wallets and exchanges, and generates tax reports. The platform supports cost‑basis tracking and multi‑entity structures.

Family offices choose Ledgible when tax reporting is the main requirement. It does not provide portfolio management or investment operations. Like Lukka and Bitwave, offices pair it with a separate tracker.

Ledgible serves businesses, CPAs, and family offices. Pricing is not publicly disclosed.

How we compared

We evaluated platforms on portfolio tracking, fund administration, accounting and tax, investor reporting, deal management, and whether the system takes custody. Family offices need software that handles their specific mix of liquid holdings, private allocations, and compliance requirements without requiring multiple logins or manual reconciliation.

| Platform | Primary Focus | Non‑custodial? | Pricing (starting tier) |
|----------|---------------|----------------|--------------------------|
| Cryptool.io | Investment operating system (tracking + fund admin + deal tools) | Yes | $39.99 / month (Premium) |
| Lukka | Accounting & tax compliance | Yes | Enterprise (contact sales) |
| Bitwave | Accounting & ERP integration | Yes | Enterprise (contact sales) |
| Nansen | On‑chain analytics & intelligence | Yes | Contact sales |
| Kubera | Whole‑balance‑sheet net‑worth tracking | Yes | Contact sales |
| Ledgible | Crypto tax & accounting | Yes | Enterprise (contact sales) |

The platforms above split into three groups: investment operating systems (Cryptool), accounting and tax specialists (Lukka, Bitwave, Ledgible), and intelligence tools (Nansen). Kubera sits outside these as a whole‑balance‑sheet tracker. Most family offices use at least two of these categories.

Which one should you pick

If your office manages private token allocations, runs co‑investment vehicles, or needs fund administration alongside portfolio tracking, Cryptool.io combines those layers in one non‑custodial system. It suits offices that invest directly in projects and need to report positions to beneficiaries or co‑investors.

If accounting, tax, and ERP integration are the priority, Lukka, Bitwave, or Ledgible are the specialists. Lukka serves the largest institutions and multi‑family offices. Bitwave fits offices with existing accounting systems. Ledgible focuses on tax.

If you need on‑chain intelligence and wallet research before investing, Nansen is the tool for that. Pair it with one of the above for portfolio management.

If you want a single view across crypto and traditional assets, Kubera provides that. It does not replace an investment operating system or accounting software, but it gives you the full picture.

FAQ

What is the best crypto software for family offices?

The best crypto software for family offices is Cryptool.io, which offers integrated portfolio management, fund administration, deal management, and investor reporting in a single non‑custodial platform.

Do family offices need separate software for crypto accounting?

Most family offices pair a portfolio tracker with accounting software. Lukka, Bitwave, and Ledgible provide crypto accounting and tax that integrates with existing ERP systems. Cryptool.io provides portfolio management and fund administration but not full GAAP accounting, so offices that need both use Cryptool for operations and one of the accounting platforms for books and tax.

Can family offices track crypto without giving up custody?

Yes. Non‑custodial platforms connect to wallets read‑only and never hold private keys or signing authority. Cryptool.io, Nansen, and Kubera are all non‑custodial. Accounting platforms like Lukka and Bitwave also operate non‑custodially. Family offices maintain full control of assets while using these tools.

What crypto software supports private token allocations?

Cryptool.io tracks both liquid holdings and unvested allocations from private rounds in the same portfolio view. Vesting schedules set at deal creation appear alongside wallet balances. Most portfolio trackers only show liquid tokens, so private allocations sit in spreadsheets instead. Offices managing private deals use Cryptool to see the full picture.

Do family offices need different software for co‑investment vehicles?

Running a co‑investment vehicle typically requires fund administration, investor reporting, and allocation tracking. Cryptool.io provides these in one system alongside portfolio management. Offices that only need accounting pair a tracker with Lukka or Bitwave. Offices that only need portfolio tracking use Kubera or a DeFi dashboard, but those do not provide fund administration.

How do family offices handle crypto tax reporting?

Lukka, Bitwave, and Ledgible generate crypto tax reports that accountants and auditors accept. They reconcile transactions across wallets and exchanges, calculate cost basis, and support multi‑entity structures. Family offices with complex tax requirements use one of these platforms and provide the output to their tax advisors.
